components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The compact default action for grading, saving, and proceeding.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { min-height: 34px; padding: 8px 14px; border: 1px solid var(--navy, #12233f); border-radius: 3px; background: var(--navy, #12233f); color: var(--panel, #fffdf8); font: 500 14px/1.2 "IBM Plex Sans", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: transform .15s ease, background .18s ease, border-color .18s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-1px); background: var(--accent, #8b2635); border-color: var(--accent, #8b2635); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid rgba(139,38,53,.32); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Academic Search Field
components.description: A keyboard-first search field for chapters, topics, and maintained sources.
components.html: <label class="ds-search"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" aria-hidden="true"><circle cx="10.5" cy="10.5" r="6.5"/><path d="m15.5 15.5 5 5"/></svg><input type="search" placeholder="Find a chapter or topic"></label>

components.name: Active Navigation Item

components.html: Dashboard

narrative.overview:
Wicker Study is a durable academic instrument rather than a conventional dashboard. Its interface borrows the composure of a university press catalogue and the utility of a supervised reading room: source material is visually primary, navigation behaves like a folio index, and personal progress appears as a precise marginal record.

The system is editorial, compact, and restrained. Warm paper fields, decisive typographic contrast, fine rules, and rare institutional color organize dense material without turning every datum into a card. Refero informs the discipline of selecting proven interaction patterns for each workflow; its gallery interface is not a visual template.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial hierarchy carried by type, rules, and whitespace rather than decorative containers.
One institutional navigation rail plus a contextual folio rail only when an outline is necessary.
Dense registers and ledgers for progress, mistakes, mock history, and course navigation.
Controlled reading measures with quiet marginal study tools.
Oxblood used sparingly for action, location, and focus; navy carries institutional structure.

rules.name: The Rare Mark Rule
rules.body: Oxblood identifies action, location, or authorship; it never washes large decorative areas.

rules.name: The Paper Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Reading Leaf holds authored material, Warm Stock holds the workspace, and Field Paper groups controls or metadata.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif explains and names, sans-serif operates, and mono records; do not swap their jobs for novelty.

rules.name: The Reading Measure Rule
rules.body: Authored prose stops at 70ch even when the application uses the full viewport.

rules.name: The One Permanent Rail Rule
rules.body: Never place a second global menu beside the institutional rail; only task-local outlines qualify for a contextual rail.

rules.name: The Full Workspace Rule
rules.body: Cap reading measure, not application width. Wide screens should improve comparison and tool access rather than add blank margins.

rules.name: The Flat Ledger Rule
rules.body: Repeated information is divided by rules, never lifted into a grid of floating cards.

rules.name: The Folio Edge Rule
rules.body: Ordinary containers do not become soft rounded cards; curvature belongs to controls and the authored Wicker mark.

dos: Do make authored material the largest, quietest, and most readable surface.
Do use ruled rows and aligned columns for repeated academic records.
Do preserve exact source, chapter, page, percentage, and timestamp data in the mono voice.
Do use the full desktop width while protecting the 70ch reading measure.
Do provide visible keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, and a purposeful compact mobile rail.
donts: Don't rebuild dense workflows as equal rounded cards or nested bordered panels.
Don't add a second permanent course navigator beside the global rail.
Don't use Oxblood as decorative background acreage or navy as an indiscriminate content fill.
Don't mix serif, sans-serif, and mono roles arbitrarily.
Don't copy Refero's own gallery appearance; use it to study proven product flow patterns.
